articles.title: ¿El mes de noviembre tiene feriados? Revisa cuáles son los días NO laborables en Perú
articles.summary: El calendario peruano de 2026 contempla fechas especiales durante noviembre. Conoce cuántos feriados quedan este mes, qué días se celebran y si habrá jornadas de descanso para los trabajadores del sector público y privado.
articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

articles.title: Is Jensen Huang’s bad behavior more commonplace than it seems? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: “There are a lot of senior people in the industry that know this is happening, and are effectively condoning it,” an investment intel consultant said.
articles.body_text: The AI industry is still reeling from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s honeypot scandal, but some in the industry see it as an issue that’s much larger than one man. The Chinese government has been active in economic espionage for decades, and with semiconductors at the center of the AI boom, there’s intense pressure to infiltrate any company involved. At the same time, many of the executives getting rich off that boom have made themselves easy targets. As CEO of investment intel firm Heron Intelligence, Nate Singer has a unique view into the problem. His firm works on corporate due diligence: Essentially, making sure companies know the relevant dirt before making a major acquisition or executive hire. And while the Nvidia case is particularly severe, Singer says there are lots of similar cases in the semiconductor industry that have stayed under the radar. “We’ve got former employees talking about behavior at senior executive levels,” Singer told TechCrunch, saying executives are “really crossing lines that should not be crossed.” In a widely circulated LinkedIn post , Singer detailed one case in which a CEO’s wife made an unexpected board room appearance, “screaming about her husband and another company exec flying around in the corporate jet with a couple young ladies (who also turned out to be state-sponsored actors).” It’s an alarming story, but an unfortunately common one. Singer says he’s seen at least three reports of similar cases, and suspects many more have gone unreported. “There’s a lot more than this one woman,” Singer said. “They are embedded in these companies.” Semiconductor companies are already big targets for international trade secret theft. There have been dozens of prosecutions for similar cases in recent years, including a case involving the fabrication powerhouse TSMC in 2006. In 2017, four executives at an unnamed “Bay Area semiconductor equipment manufacturer” were charged with stealing trade secrets for use at a competing company in China. According to the indictment, the technology in question “related to the high-volume manufacturing of semiconductor wafers to be used in lighting and electronic devices, such as flat screen televisions and smart phones.“ Any sexual elements in such cases rarely become public, in part because of the severe consequences for executives and their companies. But according to Singer, the ongoing threat has become a kind of open secret in the industry. “There are a lot of senior people in the industry that know this is happening, and are effectively condoning it,” he told TechCrunch. articles.title: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sales of $10B represents an almost 50% jump from revenue of $6.7 billion the company recorded in the second quarter.
articles.body_text: OpenAI is bouncing back from the doldrums it experienced earlier this year. The company’s quarterly revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time, thanks to strong demand for its recent AI models, Bloomberg reported, citing anonymous sources. If true, that would represent an almost 50% jump from the $6.7 billion in sales the company reportedly recorded in the second quarter. That would also mark a sizable increase in its revenue growth rate, which was previously said to be about 18% between the first and second quarters of the year. OpenAI’s profitability picture also appears to have improved, with its adjusted operating margin narrowing from -150% in the second quarter to -109% in the third quarter, the report said. OpenAI, one of the first to commercialize AI models, wasn’t exactly struggling to continue growing its top-line expansion — 18% growth on top of $5.7 billion in quarterly revenue is massive by any measure, especially compared to most software businesses. Still, the company lagged Anthropic in catering to enterprises, a market where the Claude-maker has pulled ahead, at least in terms of revenue growth. OpenAI has recently benefited from a combination of tighter pricing, discounts, improving models, and a greater focus on building more enterprise-focused products and AI agents that can help people complete tasks. OpenAI has now reached an annual revenue run rate of $50 billion, according to Bloomberg. Meanwhile, Anthropic, which is seeking a $1.4 trillion valuation in an IPO likely to happen soon , said yesterday that its annual revenue run rate had increased by $10 billion within a month to $81 billion as of the end of October. (Note that OpenAI and Anthropic calculate their annualized revenue differently: Anthropic counts sales made by its cloud partners, while OpenAI only reports its share of some sales through its partners.) None of those figures are small, of course, but the companies are also competing with models from Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, as well as a plethora of cheaper but still highly capable models from open-source AI labs, especially those from China. articles.title: Siri co-founder backs Helix for its voice ID tech | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Helix said that its voice ID tech can run on an iPhone 13
articles.body_text: For years, websites have relied on technology like CAPTCHA to prove that the user on the other end is human. More recently, social media platforms have turned to photos or videos to verify users’ identities. Now, a startup called Helix is betting that voice technology can do the same job, without requiring users to hand over sensitive personal information. The voice technology, which can run directly on a user’s device, has attracted backing from Siri co-founder Dag Kittlaus, who will also act as an advisor. The company raised $6 million in funding in a round led by Chicago Ventures, with participation from BAM Ventures, Aglaé Ventures, Corazon Capital, Tusk Ventures, Yonder Ventures, Rule30, and Brown Alumni Group. The startup was founded by Alex Oberg, Anna Dorofiyenko, and Mike Hall in 2025. Oberg previously worked at Ticketmaster, which acquired his startup; Dorofiyenko led data science teams at Live Nation and Zillow; and Hall has worked at Nike and Tinder, where he helped develop the initial matching algorithm. At Ticketmaster, Oberg played a role in creating Verified Fan, which is designed to keep bots out of the platform. As AI advanced, he started thinking along the same lines for a new solution. “As AI started to come up in the last two years, I was realizing that it’s going to make it increasingly difficult to determine who’s human and who’s not on the Internet. Identity on the Internet’s always been about proxies for identity, right? It’s your email, it’s your phone, it’s your IP address, it’s your device fingerprint, it’s your device ID,” Oberg said. He noted that with the rise of AI agents like Instinct and Muse, the industry needs to rethink human identity on the internet and rely on biometric signals like voice, which is where Helix comes in. Its core technology can run directly on a device to determine whether someone is human and estimate their age. The company is also running pilots to explore whether voice can be used a biomarker to detect conditions such as adrunkenness or distress. The company can deploy its technology to replace or supplement CAPTCHA and help block bot attacks. Helix said that because its model can run locally even on an iPhone 13, the cost of deploying the technology is minimal. The startup said one of its customers is Zeel, an in-home healthcare provider that uses Helix’s tech to verify the identities of providers visiting customers’ homes. The CEO also emphasized the limitations of Helix’s technology, noting that it cannot reliably detect whether someone is lying. He added that its voice technology doesn’t identify individual speakers and claimed that even if the company stores a voiceprint, it cannot be used to reconstruct a person’s voice. AI-powered fraud is also a growing problem in phone calls. But Helix believes its technology isn’t yet capable of reliably detecting AI agents during live calls. Siri co-founder Kittlaus said that voice identification technology has finally reached a point where it works reliably, positioning Helix to scale as AI-powered fraud increases. He also said that Helix’s work to compress its models gives the startup a cost advantage.

articles.title: Databricks' new AI agent tells CEO Ali Ghodsi the unvarnished truth | TechCrunch
articles.summary: At 12,000 employees, AI Ghodsi is the first to admit that he can't know everyone and that they are unlikely to confess the things that go wrong to him. But he doesn't need them to. He uses Databricks' newly revised Genie agent for that.
articles.body_text: Databricks on Wednesday unveiled an updated version of its AI agent Genie, which can now perform multi-step jobs that take extended work to finish. It does this through an ontology that Databricks built to give Genie the context it needs from the information that customers store on the Databricks platform. Corporate leaders can now assign the agent a wide range of tasks, and it will complete them unsupervised, the company says. To prove the point, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi showed me how he uses it internally. Instead of a product demo, he fired up his actual agent and walked me through his most recent chats and charts. He showed me how it analyzed the parts of an employee satisfaction survey where the company didn’t score well, and how it helped him rate (and discard) fixes for those low scores that some executives suggested. He showed me how it summarized a big sales pitch to a prospect that went poorly — including the features the prospect said it needed before buying. It also prepped him for a podcast interview by reviewing his previous appearances and developing likely questions. While we talked, he even had it tell him what he should say to me. (And its advice on that wasn’t bad.) The fascinating part was that Ghodsi was using Genie to find the stuff that he’s now unlikely to hear as the big boss. It was a source of unvarnished truth about what wasn’t going well that he needed to address. “Have you heard of Dunbar’s number? The magic number is 150,” he said when I pointed this out. Named for British anthropologist Robin Dunbar, it’s theoretically the maximum number of people with whom humans can maintain stable relationships. In a small startup, a CEO knows everyone, has direct relationships with them, and they feel safe to tell him negative info straight up. With 12,000 employees, Ghodsi is the first to admit he can’t know everyone. At that size, a salesperson isn’t likely to confess a disastrous sales call to the CEO. An HR manager isn’t likely to confess that their idea for increasing employee satisfaction will probably fail. “Anyone who has more than 150 employees, which is a lot of companies, a lot of people can get value out of this,” he said of AI agents generally and his product, Genie, specifically. Ghodsi’s own use of Genie (often called dogfooding, from the phrase “eating your own dogfood”) is one reason why Databricks is now pitching it as an always-on agent for business leaders. He says he also uses it in his personal life, rather than a security-questionable alternative like OpenClaw or Instinct or Muse. He believes Genie can do for the business side what AI, agents and harnesses (the software that wraps around an AI model and lets it use tools) are doing for programmers. As for the risk that agents will ratchet up corporate AI costs, Ghodsi has an answer for that, too. He said costs can be controlled through Databricks’ Unity Gateway product. It allows companies to set usage limits and to swap in less expensive open-weight models. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Plurai wants to help AI agents work better using the same approach that helped get self-driving cars to roads | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Like the end-to-end models trained to drive cars, AI agents are probabilistic systems operating in unpredictable environments.
articles.body_text: AI agents are all the rage, but they’re not quite as capable as their purveyors would have you believe. Efforts to benchmark agents tasked with complex work show that they aren’t typically reliable enough to function without close supervision. LiveBench 2.0 shows Claude Fable 5.2 and ChatGPT-6 Astra succeeding on 82.9 and 75.6 out of 100 tasks, respectively, and an effort by the AI infrastructure company EON to test agents in a simulated corporate environment found the most successful model tested, Claude Opus 4.8, performed tasks at 76.8% accuracy. Now, a startup known as Plurai wants to boost those numbers with the same techniques that put self-driving cars on the street: Simulations using synthetic data based on a company’s own digital systems, meant to prepare models to tackle difficult edge cases. Co-founders Ilan Kadar and Elad Levi previously worked for Nexar, which develops autonomous driving technology. Kadar worked with Waymo to simulate and evaluate its end-to-end deep learning driving software. “The moment that we saw the wave of AI agents, we saw the same pattern: That it is very easy to build a demo, but [hard] to get something that will be reliable and cost effective,” Kadar told TechCrunch. “Since we saw the same pattern, the same pitch was that we want to build this simulation layer.” On Wednesday, the startup said it had raised $13 million in seed funding to make that happen. The round was led by Team8, with participation from U&I, Velocity and Mercer. Like the end-to-end models trained to drive cars, AI agents are probabilistic systems operating in unpredictable environments. When pressed by customers, agents tasked with booking travel can ignore spending policies. Or, when tasked with querying one database, agents can reliably provide an answer, but combining information from multiple data sets tends to gum up the works. A long conversation with a customer service bot can overwhelm an agent with too much context and lead to wrong turns. To fix that, Plurai creates a digital twin of the company’s electronic systems, including the knowledge base and tools that an agent will have access to in production. It then maps all the possible flows of the agents, and uses that graph to prepare the model with evaluations and fixes for possible edge cases. The platform works alongside existing agentic tools like Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and Cursor. However, Kadar says the company’s real promise is using the data it gathers to post-train small, open-weight models tailored to individual customer needs. Tests performed in cooperation with Nvidia and Nebius showed the company’s models outperforming mid-tier frontier models at lower costs. “We can take a large language model, we can take the task, decompose it into a smaller task using the simulation, train [an open-weight] model, and using the simulation, verify that the quality is higher or comparable to the frontier model, and an order or two orders of magnitude cost reduction,” he said. Reah Miyara, a Google DeepMind researcher who backed Plurai as an angel investor, said the company’s edge comes from understanding failure modes in production, and generating synthetic data to tune models. As businesses try to optimize their AI expense, Plurai’s approach could prove a real advantage, since IT leaders are seeing that “frontier-capable models are out of distribution with my specific data, and the cost of these things isn’t sustainable in the long term,” Miyara said. Plurai hopes analogies between AI agents in physical and digital environments can prove predictive: While powerful general AI models are imbuing robots with fascinating capabilities, they aren’t yet reliable enough to be deployed widely. Meanwhile, robots powered by AI models built for specific tasks are in the field right now, working for customers and gathering valuable real-world data.

articles.title: Nvidia’s crisis has corporate governance experts reaching for the popcorn | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The governance experts we talked to say nobody has seen anything like what's unfolding right now.
articles.body_text: Nvidia’s stock sank 5.47% on Tuesday, following a 4% drop on Monday, a loss of about 9.5% in two days, even though there wasn’t much news out of the company. CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly been trying to conduct business as usual after admitting to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The biggest development: the board hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an internal investigation. What comes next is mostly a guessing game, even for the people who study how boards are supposed to handle crises. Two corporate governance professors, Ann Lipton of the University of Colorado and Todd Henderson of the University of Chicago, say there is no real precedent for a CEO caught up in a suspected honeypot. And while they have views on what the investigation should ask, like everyone else, they’re watching to see how it plays out. “There have actually been affair cases and sexual harassment cases,” Lipton said, but was quick to add that she doesn’t know of previous cases that also involve potential national security compromises. Henderson, whose research interests include corporations, securities regulation, and law and economics, said much depends on facts few people have yet, including, most importantly, what, if anything, Alice Huang got out of Jensen Huang. (Secrets about Nvidia’s fabs or chip designs would matter to the Justice Department. Ordinary corporate information probably would not.) Lipton described the investigation led by Nvidia’s independent board members, with their own outside counsel, as perhaps the most “standard” aspect of the whole affair so far. She also observed that an investigation will be “exactly as thorough” as the directors running it want it to be, which is also standard. Henderson made a related point about incentives, saying that Washington law firms that conduct internal investigations “know who pays their bills.” He didn’t suggest that’s happening here. Lipton said she sees three lines of inquiry, including whether the law was broken, whether Huang violated Nvidia’s internal policies, and whether the board was misled, including how forthcoming he was and when he was on notice. It’s notable, as Wired reported Monday , that Huang hired a PR crisis firm known for handling sex scandals a full year ago. Of course, the driver could have been about the affair alone. It’s unclear when Huang learned Alice Huang was a suspected spy. The board said in a Sunday statement about the matter that Nvidia has “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” Henderson similarly stressed the importance of what Huang knew and when. He described two scenarios. In one, Huang hires a PR firm because an extramarital affair is embarrassing, without knowing who the woman is. In the other, he knows she is a suspected Chinese spy. “I think that’s very different,” he said. “If I were a board member and the CEO of a company with very sensitive technology was in that situation, I would be furious if they didn’t tell me.” Not telling the board that you have cancer “or that you’ve been sleeping with a Chinese spy,” said Henderson, “seems to me to be a fireable offense.” Either way, Lipton expects shareholder suits, and she said two kinds are possible. Securities fraud, which she said is “only about lying,” is the most obvious, and as we reported yesterday, Nvidia is already facing a proposed class action lawsuit that alleges Nvidia and Huang misled investors by concealing Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang while describing dealings with her former employer as routine. “You can have as many affairs with Chinese spies as you like,” Lipton said. “You just can’t lie about it under the federal securities laws.” A mismanagement claim under Delaware law, where Nvidia is incorporated, is much harder. Employees do “stupid or reckless or damaging things all the time,” she said, and courts don’t let shareholders sue each time. Shareholders bringing such a claim on the company’s behalf, known as a derivative suit, must first show the board is incapable of handling the problem, usually by proving directors are implicated or so beholden to the CEO that they can’t act independently. Nvidia’s 10-member board has a track record of loyalty and deference to Huang, as outlined by a New York Times piece Tuesday morning. Still, the investigation those “independent” directors have announced with outside counsel makes that very hard. Lipton cited, for example, a shareholder suit over alleged mismanagement at McDonald’s several years ago, after its chief people officer was accused of harassment and its CEO had a relationship with a subordinate. Ultimately, the court found no reason the board couldn’t deal with the misconduct on its own. Even if none of this ends up threatening Huang’s job, the episode raises other governance questions that don’t look great in retrospect. Nvidia is run with a famously flat structure, with more than 60 direct reports to Huang, and the company doesn’t appear to have a succession plan, which Lipton called “a danger for any company.” Huang’s children also work at Nvidia. His son Spencer is a director of product management, his daughter Madison is a senior director of product marketing, and his son-in-law, Nico Caprez, works in business development. Some employees believe he is grooming successors, and asked last month by Bloomberg whether Madison is in line for the job, Huang didn’t shoot down the idea, saying instead that it’s not something he’d wish on her. Lipton called hiring the kids poor corporate hygiene, even though founders have long done it. (Kimbal Musk is on Tesla’s board because he’s Elon Musk’s brother, she noted.) Directors are supposed to act only for stockholders, but founders get more rope as long as the company is thriving.

articles.title: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI has not yet said what its plans are for the future of travel. But Sonder founder Francis Davidson is a well-known figure in the travel industry.
articles.body_text: OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to Odessia’s founder, Francis Davidson. Davidson says in a post announcing the deal that he’s now working for OpenAI, helping the AI lab with the future of travel. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but this looks like an acqui-hire. Davidson’s announcement focused largely on how he built his AI travel agent Odessia by directing teams of AI agents. The year-old Odessia raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia and launched its AI travel agent around five months ago. Davidson says that it had helped early adopters plan millions of dollars’ worth of travel, but the tool has already been shut down. An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed the hire to TechCrunch. “We’re thrilled to welcome Francis to OpenAI. Francis is a proven founder who has built multiple businesses to help people travel, and we’re excited he’s chosen to build with us.” However the AI lab has not announced new travel-specific products or plans. It does, however, count such companies as Bookings.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners. Travel is also one of the main areas that people are using personal AI assistants to help with. And, back in July 2025, when OpenAI launched its ChatGPT agent , it mentioned travel as one of its potential uses. OpenAI’s spokesperson didn’t have more to share on its plans for travel-related products, except to say that travel is one of the areas that chatbot users frequently ask about. “1.2 billion people turn to ChatGPT each week for help with everyday tasks — from understanding their health, figuring out what to make for dinner, building a budget, and even planning a trip. We see a real opportunity to make these experiences even more useful,” the spokesperson said. Acquiring Odessia is interesting for another reason. Davidson is well known in the travel industry after he founded a travel startup called Sonder as a college student in 2014. It was sort of like Airbnb, but it focused on short-term leasing of upscale apartments in major cities worldwide. The pandemic badly hurt it, and as it climbed out of that rut, it went public via a SPAC but didn’t raise as much money as it needed, Davidson later said in a post announcing his resignation as CEO in June 2025. When a key partnership with Marriott fell through , the company went into bankruptcy and wound down. The bankruptcy trustee sold Sonder’s name, trademarks, and website domain in 2026 to TravelAI, and that website operates as a curated guide to the kind of travel rental properties that Sonder was once known for. Prior to its downfall, Davidson had built Sonder into a unicorn with $143 million in revenues. While Sonder was not, ultimately, a success story, Davidson is the kind of battle-scarred founder that Silicon Valley often values. So we’ll have to wait and see what OpenAI has in store now with travel, now that he’s joined the company. Note: This story was updated with OpenAI’s comments. articles.title: Proximal Ventures raises debut fund to back startups bringing AI to drug development | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Former SignalFire investor Sahir Raoof raises $27.5 million for new fund targeting AI in pharma.
articles.body_text: While established venture firms continue to attract capital, first-time fund managers are facing one of the toughest fundraising environments in years. But that didn’t stop Sahir Raoof, a former SignalFire investor and executive at two healthcare startups, from raising $27.5 million for his first solo VC fund. Raoof’s firm, Proximal Ventures , is betting that AI can transform the tools, infrastructure, and services that support drug development. Pharmaceutical companies have historically outsourced various stages of drug development to specialized service providers, from synthesizing thousands of molecular compounds and figuring out how to manufacture drugs at scale to analyzing clinical trial data. “For a long time, the assumption was that pharma is not a great buyer of software, but a really good buyer of services,” Raoof told TechCrunch. Raoof believes AI could automate much of that work, creating an opportunity for startups to capture billions of dollars in pharmaceutical industry spending. By using AI, these companies could deliver the same services at a lower cost and in significantly less time, he said. Some of the most valuable applications of AI so far have been in service-oriented industries like law and finance, Raoof said. He sees similar opportunities in pharmaceutical services. Proximal plans to invest in pre-seed and seed-stage startups, writing checks from $500,000 to $1.5 million. The firm has already backed seven startups, including ChronicleBio, co-founded by former OpenAI executive Fidji Simo, which uses AI to analyze biological and medical data to better understand chronic diseases and identify potential treatments. Before spending two years as a principal at SignalFire, Raoof led business development at clinical trial recruitment startup Iterative Health and previously oversaw partnerships at Flatiron Health, an oncology data company acquired by Roche for $1.9 billion in 2018. “If you’re building a company that’s selling into the life sciences, one of the hardest things to do is starting that initial commercial flywheel,” Raoof said. His sales chops, deep understanding of the healthcare ecosystem, and extensive industry relationships gave limited partners, the investors in VC funds, the confidence that he could spot strong startups and help them land customers. Proximal’s backers include VC firms SignalFire and Kleiner Perkins, Bertelsmann Healthcare Investments, and individual investors such as Dimension Capital co-founders Nan Li and Zavain Dar. Amy Abernethy, co-founder of Highlander Health and former principal deputy commissioner of the FDA, is also an investor. She first met Raoof when they worked together at Flatiron Health, where she served as chief medical officer. She told TechCrunch that his ability to build relationships and spot industry bottlenecks made a lasting impression. Abernethy is convinced that his abilities, along with the understanding of what the healthcare market needs, will make him a successful investor. It is these qualities that have helped Proximal invest in startups alongside some of the better-known, much larger funds, she added.

articles.title: X-energy gets green light to build its first small modular nuclear reactors | TechCrunch
articles.summary: X-energy received a construction permit from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission to build four reactors in Texas.
articles.body_text: Nuclear startup X-energy announced Monday that it had been given the go-ahead from federal officials to build its first four commercial reactors. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) approved the construction permit application for four of X-energy’s Xe-100 reactors at a Dow chemical plant in Texas. Each reactor will be capable of generating 80 megawatts of electricity and 200 megawatts of heat. X-energy says the approval is the first for an advanced nuclear reactor at an industrial site in the United States. The U.S. nuclear industry has pinned its hopes on small modular reactors — or SMRs — like those being developed by X-energy. By shrinking the reactor, proponents say it will speed construction and reduce costs, though those advantages have yet to be proven. No SMR is currently in operation in the U.S., and X-energy says Dow’s reactors won’t be operational until the early 2030s. X-energy claims that its reactor design, which flows helium gas over uranium-containing fuel pellets, is safer than many existing reactors, but the Union of Concerned Scientists questioned the claim and the speed with which X-energy received the permit. “The NRC only accomplished this feat by pushing consideration of critical safety questions to a later date—issues the NRC should’ve fully resolved before green lighting construction,” Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety for the organization, said in a statement. The nuclear industry has benefited from strong interest from hyperscalers and data center developers, who are desperate for any and all sources of electricity. Amazon’s Climate Pledge Fund led X-energy’s $500 million Series C-1 , and the big tech company has also committed to buying 5 gigawatts of capacity from the nuclear startup. X-energy rode that wave of excitement earlier this year when its April initial public offering raised $1 billion. But since then, investors’ optimism has tempered. The hesitancy isn’t surprising: Nuclear power plants are expensive to build and can take years to complete. Eventually, X-energy hopes to rein in both time and cost, but its first reactors are likely to be pricey. The new permit approval gave X-energy a small jolt yesterday, though it was only enough to recover last week’s losses. The company’s shares are trading at less than half their initial offering price. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor. De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College.

articles.title: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Each of the seven co-founders plans to sell exactly the same number of shares in the IPO, which would bring each of them about $250 million in cash at the midpoint of the price range while leaving the group in control of the company.
articles.body_text: As Anthropic barrels toward an enormous IPO that could value it at $1.4 trillion, the company has disclosed a tidbit in its new S-1 filing about how many shares each of its seven co-founders plan to sell. Each will sell 3,378,378 shares. Anthropic has floated an unusually broad initial price range of $70 to $78 a share. At the midrange of $74, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million. At the low end, $70, each would have to settle for pocketing just over $236 million in cash; at the high end, $78, each would take in just under $264 million. However, in an IPO as eagerly anticipated as this one, companies can often price shares above the initial range. The S-1 is already hinting at high demand. Board member Reed Hastings has indicated he wants to buy $300 million worth of shares through his donor-advised fund. Board member Christopher Liddell also wants to buy $3 million worth of shares. The seven co-founders are Dario Amodei, CEO; Daniela Amodei, president and chair of the board; Tom Brown, chief compute officer; Jack Clark, head of public benefit; Jared Kaplan, chief science officer (pictured above); Sam McCandlish, chief architect; and Christopher Olah, interpretability research lead. After the sale, each of them will own about 3.2% of the total outstanding Class A shares, the S-1 says, or roughly 22% collectively. That’s not their share of the company overall. Class A is just one of Anthropic’s share classes, and other holders, including Amazon and Google, hold nonvoting Class N shares, so the founders’ stake in the company’s total equity will be considerably smaller. Even still, they, as a group, remain in control of the company. Each will also receive one share of Class F stock, which carries supervoting rights. Collectively, the founders will control 51.1% of the votes, but no single founder will hold significantly more shares or votes than the others. As is now industry lore, the seven left OpenAI to start Anthropic in 2021 after disagreements with OpenAI’s leadership over how AI should be built. Siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, who held senior research and policy roles at OpenAI, were joined by five fellow OpenAI colleagues in forming a company that has said, very publicly and from the start, that it’s more focused on AI safety than its rivals, including the founders’ former employer. articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild review
articles.summary: Link’s latest adventure is a bold and much-needed reinvention of the beloved franchise
articles.body_text: The moment I realized The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild might actually be my favorite Zelda adventure ever struck me like lightning — literally. While running through the picturesque green fields of Hyrule, a massive storm unexpectedly rolled in. As heavy rain began to pour, a strong wind rustled the tall grass, and in the distance I could hear the crack of lightning. The sharp sound rapidly came closer and closer until zap! I was electrocuted to death by a bolt. Every time I restarted, the same thing would happen. I couldn’t understand why the lightning was targeting me, the helpless hero, until I realized that both the spear and shield on my back were made of metal. With the steel unequipped, I was able to safely make my through the storm. Breath of the Wild has something that’s been missing from the series for years: surprise. Most recent Zelda adventures have become formulaic, abiding by a rigid and proven structure that offers nostalgia and familiarity, but little room for revelations, either big or small. Breath of the Wild is more open and natural than its predecessors, letting you discover things — like how lightning works — through experimentation. It isn’t always as curated and cinematic as other Zelda games, but the unpredictability makes it feel like a true adventure, where you’re uncovering your own path, instead of hitting your marks and following the script. Zelda games have always been large, but Breath of the Wild feels uniquely grand, a massive open world filled with so much to do that I suspect most players — even those who complete the main story — will miss large swaths of the map. The scale could have been daunting, but the joy of discovery and the satisfaction that comes from finding your own way make it inviting instead. I want to go the places I’ve yet to discover. I want to uncover new secrets and abilities. I want more. At 50 hours into the game, I still haven’t reached the end of Breath of the Wild. In some ways it feels like I’ve only scratched the surface. But even still, these bold changes have profoundly altered my expectations of what a Zelda adventure can be. And I’m entirely convinced that this is the best Zelda game I’ve ever played. This review contains light spoilers for the early hours of Breath of the Wild. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/8079395/NintendoSwitch_TLOZBreathoftheWild_Presentation2017_scrn34_png_jpgcopy.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Breath of the Wild opens with series hero Link awakening in a dark cavern. A mysterious disembodied voice guides him to a tablet that has a passing resemblance to both the Switch and Nintendo’s maligned Wii U controller. The tablet helps to navigate this version of Hyrule — the fantasy realm that has long been the heart of Zelda adventures. As you learn in the very early parts of the game, a century ago, powerful evil destroyed much of the world, allowing nature to reclaim castles, and littering the land with abandoned machines of war. People still exist, in small towns and stables, but much of Hyrule is beset by hordes of monsters who have bivouacked into the hills. This is a dangerous place. Naturally, your job is to set things right. One of the game’s greatest strengths is how it goes about explaining how you will do that — or just as often, not explaining it. Breath of the Wild rarely gives you explicit directions as to what to do. Instead, it tells (or shows) you what needs to happen, and lets you fill in the rest. One line of quests tasks you with uncovering shrines (more on those later) using only lines from a poem or a riddle as guidance. Another presents a series of images of scenic Hyrule locations from before the calamity, and asks you to find them as they are now. In order to defeat Ganon you’ll need to first uncover four “divine beasts” scattered throughout the world. Of course, the game doesn’t even tell you what a divine beast is. This lack of direction can be disorienting at first. I played Breath of the Wild immediately after finishing another huge role-playing game, Horizon Zero Dawn, and it was a jarring transition. After spending 40 hours playing a game that literally pointed me in the right direction at all times, now I was forced to fend for myself. But it very quickly turned into a liberating sensation. Instead of worrying if I was following the correct path, for the first dozen hours or so, I largely ignored the story altogether. Instead, I trekked across Hyrule activating the specific towers found in each region, which not only help fill in the details of the map but also provide crucial fast-travel points. Even the act of filling out Breath of the Wild’s map instils a deep sense of adventure. In most open-world games, particularly Ubisoft titles like Far Cry or Assassin’s Creed, your map is overburdened with icons from the very beginning. You can spot where everything from a city to a treasure chest is located before you even start exploring. It can feel overwhelming. Breath of the Wild, meanwhile, does the opposite. When you first start out, the map is almost completely empty. You can see the dividing lines between the various regions that make up Hyrule, but none of their details. It’s only once you start exploring that it fills out. A town won’t appear on your map until you actually go there, which you can only do by finding it on your own. Discovering a new place or thing truly feels like an act of discovery. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/8079407/NintendoSwitch_TLOZBreathoftheWild_Presentation2017_scrn31_png_jpgcopy.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Breath of the Wild features two significant additions that completely changed how I viewed the world around me. In addition to the usual methods of traversal — foot, horse, and fast travel — Link now also has the ability to climb nearly every surface you come across. If you spot a mountain, a castle, or virtually anything else, you can climb it. The only restriction is Link’s stamina — which expands over time and can be augmented with things like potions — but even then there are ways around it if you’re clever. This marks a fundamental shift for the series. Instead of an impediment, walls and mountains are now just another potential pathway. Often I would bypass monster-plagued roads altogether and simply climb the comparatively safe mountain instead. Link’s climbing ability is made all the more useful and important by a seemingly innocuous paraglider, which lets Link temporarily soar through the air. In short order, it became a pivotal part of the game, and my main method of transportation. Instead of walking or riding to a new location, I would climb the nearest high point — a mountain, or maybe a tower — and then glide in the direction of where I wished to be. The act of getting somewhere became exciting in and of itself. There’s a certain pleasure that comes from just having enough energy to reach the top of a tower before losing your grip, or sailing peacefully above enemy camps as the monsters sleep below, unaware. Not only is Breath of the Wild’s map large; it’s also dense. I was constantly discovering new places and puzzles, both elaborate and diminutive. One of my favorite additions to the game is the shrines — glowing caverns scattered liberally across the map. Each one is like a miniature, self-contained Zelda dungeon. Early on these shrines serve as tutorials, showing necessary details about Link’s powers — like his ability to temporarily halt time or use bombs — but later they essentially become puzzle boxes, which approach Portal-levels of cleverness. The shrines also simplify the Zelda dungeon formula in an almost mobile game-like manner, resulting in satisfyingly quick puzzles that can usually be completed in less than 15 minutes or so. Even better, unlike typical Zelda puzzles, those in Breath of the Wild’s shrines often have multiple solutions. Many other additions help bring Breath of the Wild in line with contemporary open-world games like The Witcher or Skyrim, while also contributing to its overwhelming focus on adventure and discovery. Link can now cook, for instance, gathering ingredients in the wild, using them to make food that replenishes health or buffs abilities. I found myself especially taken with this feature, scouring the world for new vegetables and meats, and seeing what I could make of them. Again, cooking isn’t really explained, making it all the more compelling. Whipping up a tasty mushroom rice ball or meat-stuffed pumpkin using guesswork instead of a recipe is satisfying. I especially love the way ingredients dance and jump in the pot as you prepare a meal. There are also survival elements, forcing you to protect Link from extreme heat and cold. You’ll often find him shivering or sweating because of the weather, his health depleting. Weapons, too, give way. For the first time in a Zelda game your swords and shields degrade as you use them. But weapons are everywhere. You can even pick up a downed skeleton’s arm to bludgeon beasts, its fingers still twitching as you swing it about. Using your best equipment becomes a risky choice, not an assumption. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/8079411/NintendoSwitch_TLOZBreathoftheWild_Presentation2017_scrn05_png_jpgcopy.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Even though Breath of the Wild introduces RPG-like elements such as crafting and a greater focus on gear, it’s missing a very distinct kernel of the genre: experience. In most RPGs, numbers determine almost everything you can do. If you’re a level 5 character in a typical RPG, you definitely don’t want to head into a dungeon filled with level 10 enemies, and there’s a whole range of items and abilities you can’t use until you grind long enough to meet the appropriate level. This effectively walls off large portions of the world until you’ve achieved a numerical level of success. Breath of the Wild scraps this logic. Link gets more health and stamina as you progress, and you can acquire stronger weapons and armor, but he never gets stronger himself. He doesn’t learn to swing a sword or shoot a bow any better. But you do. Breath of the Wild offers a more open and expansive world to explore, but it also demands more of its players than other Zeldas, forcing you to get better and smarter to survive. It’s the most challenging Zelda I’ve played in many years, but also the most satisfying. (Though it never approaches the daunting difficulty of games like Bloodborne or Dark Souls.) All of these many changes fundamentally alter the Zelda formula. But what’s perhaps most remarkable about Breath of the Wild is that it still feels like a Zelda adventure — and it’s more than just the familiar setting and characters, or the stirring rendition of the Zelda theme that plays in the background. Breath of the Wild may be the biggest Zelda game to date, but it’s also an experience that distills the essence of the series into something more pure. More recent Zelda games have become bogged down with needless hand holding, an overabundance of tutorials, and overly complicated narratives. Breath of the Wild gets away from that. It changes the Zelda formula in dramatic ways, yet paradoxically it feels more Zelda than almost any game in the series before. By going big and open, Breath of the Wild gets at the heart at what a Zelda game should be. This new direction, and shaking up of the age-old formula that has come to define the series, helps Breath of the Wild return to what made Zelda so beloved in the first place. More so than just about any game series, Zelda’s heart lies in exploration, that moment of seeing a towering mountain in the distance and realizing that eventually you’ll be able to reach the top. Breath of the Wild takes this idea, cuts out the fluff, and expands upon it. It pulls ideas from other games, like crafting or survival, yet makes them feel perfectly at home in its beloved universe. It’s exactly the Zelda game I’ve been waiting for. Just watch out for lightning. The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild launches March 3rd on Nintendo Switch and Wii U.

articles.title: Åkessons ord i SVT blev ”ett uppvaknande”
articles.summary: Jimmie Åkesson (SD) kan ha satt stopp för högervinden – i Centerpartiet. Hans besked i Aktuellt har fått många att tänka om, erfar Expressen.
articles.body_text: Jimmie Åkesson (SD) kan ha satt stopp för högervinden – i Centerpartiet. Hans besked i Aktuellt har fått många att tänka om, erfar Expressen. Samtidigt uppges en majoritet av partiets riksdagsgrupp stödja ett sidbyte. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Frågan om Centerpartiets vägval är högaktuell och diskuteras just nu på en rad olika nivåer i partiet. På agendan står att avgöra om C ska välja ett samarbete med Magdalena Andersson (S), där V kan ingå i någon form, eller Ulf Kristersson (M), som lär behöva stöd av SD. Distrikten är delade i frågan och även den nya riksdagsgrupp som valdes in i september är oenig om vilket vägval som är bäst. Gruppen beskrivs av Expressens källor som ”generellt mer allianspositiv” än den som företrädde C under den gångna mandatperioden. Dagens samhälle har även pratat med flera lokalföreträdare som ställer sig bakom en sådan förflyttning. – Vi är ett borgerligt parti och har alltid varit det. Därför ser jag gärna att C sitter i en alliansregering igen, säger Ove Bengtsson (C) till tidningen. Av 25 personer i riksdagsgruppen uppges sju stycken stå bakom S-alternativet, bland dem Martin Ådahl, ekonomisk talesperson, och Birgitta Ohlsson, före detta L-profil. Exakt hur många i riksdagsgruppen som vill gå högerut är oklart, men de uppfattas vara i majoritet.

articles.title: JUST NU: Missade votering
articles.summary: Samtliga rödgröna partiledare var på plats under eftermiddagens votering – utom Centerpartiets ledare.
articles.body_text: Samtliga rödgröna partiledare var på plats under eftermiddagens votering – utom Centerpartiets ledare. ”Elisabeth kunde inte närvara vid dagens votering i riksdagen på grund av möten rörande regeringsbildningen”, skriver partiets presstjänst. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Centerpartiets ledare Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist var frånvarande vid eftermiddagens votering, som ägde rum klockan 16.00. Riksdagen röstade ja till ett antal grundlagsförändringar. Under dagen har de rödgröna partierna haft möten i Tändstickspalatset i centrala Stockholm. Vänsterpartiets vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson var tvungen att stressa i väg till riksdagen. – Vi har varit här och fått information om hur processen är tänkt framåt. Och nu måste jag tyvärr gå och rösta. – Jag tror det har varit bra, men jag måste också rösta, annars blir det saboterat i riksdagen. I övrigt var samtliga partiledare för de rödgröna på plats i kammaren – förutom en. I en kommentar till Expressen skriver Centerpartiets presstjänst: ”Elisabeth kunde inte närvara vid dagens votering i riksdagen på grund av möten rörande regeringsbildningen. Voteringarna i riksdagen är självklart viktiga, men i det här läget behöver arbetet med att hitta en väg framåt för regeringsbildningen också prioriteras.” I övrigt vill partiet inte ”kommentera i detalj”. Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist var också den enda som inte sågs till på Tändstickspalatset – dock var flera partitoppar där, som exempelvis Anders Ådahl.

articles.title: Fredssamtalen slut: ”Lösning före nyår”
articles.summary: Ryssland, USA och Ukraina har träffats i Abu Dhabi. Fredssamtal Ukrainakriget
articles.body_text: Fredssamtalen i Abu Dhabi är slut – och mycket är olöst. – Jag tycker att vi nu har en bra dynamik för att nå en lösning före nyår, säger förhandlaren David Arakhamia enligt Meduza. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Trepartssamtalen mellan Ukraina, Ryssland och USA har avslutats. Efteråt hölls en gemensam pressträff i värdstaden Abu Dhabi. Den ryska förhandlaren Vladimir Medinskij uppgav att Ryssland och Ukraina kommit överens om att utföra ett nytt ”storskaligt fångesutbyte”, enligt den oberoende ryska sajten Meduza . Även David Arakhamia, majoritetsledare i det ukrainska parlamentet som ingår i delegationen, vittnade om ”betydande framsteg” – och att Ukraina och Ryssland kan komma att nå en fredsöverenskommelse ”före nyår”. Övriga förhandlingsområden gick trögt. Speciellt frågan om territorium – som var fokus under förhandlingarnas andra dag. Som väntat nåddes inga genombrott, enligt Jared Kushner från den amerikanska delegationen. – Territoriella tvister utgör fortfarande det största hindret för ett fredsavtal, säger han på pressträffen. Samtidigt har vissa framsteg gjorts i frågan om säkerhetsgarantier, enligt Kushner. På mötet diskuterades även ett europeiskt säkerhetssystem. Där nåddes ”en ömsesidig förståelse i vissa frågor”, enligt den ryske förhandlaren Medinskij.

articles.title: Knivmördade sin vän under festnatt
articles.summary: Man får sin dom efter mord i Uppsal
articles.body_text: En lång festnatt i Uppsala i somras kulminerade när Christian Gustafsson, 30, stack kniven i magen på sin vän Tyr, 23. Skadorna gjorde att Tyr dog efter att ha förblött av sina skador. Nu döms 30-åringen till 18 års fängelse för mord. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det var tidigt på morgonen i juli som polis larmades till bostaden i Sala backe i Uppsala. Då var Tyr svårt skadad och hade förlorat stora mängder blod. Ambulanssjukvårdarna hör Tyr säga ”Krille”, vilket är Christian Gustafssons smeknamn. När polis kom dit hittade man en knivmed blod från offret och på knivskaftet hittades senare dna-spår från Christian Gustafsson som larmat och som snabbt misstänktes för mord. Flera personer befann sig i lägenheten under natten. När festkvällen eskalerade var de bara tre personer kvar. En nästan tjugo minuter lång ljudfil fångade delar av förloppet. På den hörs Christian Gustafsson säga ”Jag hugger dig”, ”jag hugger dig igen” samt offrets skrik. Rätten har beskrivit inspelningen som både hjärtskärande och blodisande. Tyr och Christian Gustafsson var bekanta med varandra sedan länge. 30-åringen har sagt att han såg Tyr som sin lillebror och att han försökte ta hand honom. Något av det sista som Tyr sa innan han blev knivhuggen var: ”Vi kommer inte slåss. Jag är vän med han”. På ljudinspelningen hörs Tyr också säga: ”Sluta fucking veva mannen” och ”Jag vill inte slå dig, du är min vän”. 30-åringen beordrade Tyr ut ur lägenheten och skrek att han skulle hugga honom om han inte försvann. Offret skulle precis gå men skulle bara hämta sin mobiltelefon. I den vevan blev 23-åringen så svårt knivhuggen att han inte överlevde. På minnessidan för Tyr har hans anhöriga lämnat några sista hälsningar. Många skriver att de minns hans skratt och hans glada, sprudlande sätt.

articles.title: Michaels olustiga fynd: ”Förbannad”
articles.summary: Grannarnas nyckel kunde öppna Michael Garderud dörr i Västra Frölunda. Flera brister har upptäckts med de digitala låsen. Nu ska Balder byta 900 lås.
articles.body_text: Michael Garderud testade en upphittad nyckel i sin ytterdörr. Den tillhörde en granne – men dörren gick upp. – Jag är rejält förbannad, säger Michael. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Grannarnas nyckel kunde öppna Michael Garderud dörr. Efter en genomgång har flera brister upptäckts med de digitala låsen på flerbostadshusen i Västra Frölunda. Nu tvingas hyresvärden Balder byta 900 lås. Det var i somras som Michael Garderud i Västra Frölunda hittade en kvarglömd nyckel i porten. Innan han lämnade tillbaka den till hyresvärden Balder, fick han en idé och testade den i sin egen ytterdörr. Dörren gick upp, något Hem & Hyra tidigare berättat om. – Vad fan är det här tänkte jag. Det blinkade rött men öppnade sig ändå, berättar, Michael Garderud. När han undersökte saken tillsammans med personal från Balder visade det sig att nyckeln tillhörde en granne flera trappor upp. Även en nyckel som tillhörde en annan grannes hemtjänstpersonal kunde öppna dörren. Låssystemet, ett elektromekaniskt lås som använder sig av fysiska nycklar med digital teknik, installerades för sju år sedan. Michael är orolig att obehöriga kan ha kunnat ta sig in i bostaden sedan dess.

articles.title: ”Ge dig inte ut i trafiken i onödan”
articles.summary: SMHI har utökat sina gula vädervarningar runtom i Sverige. Nu blir en orange. ”Ge dig inte ut i trafiken i onödan eller förbered dig på att du kan bli stillastående”, skriver SMHI.
articles.body_text: SMHI har utökat sina gula vädervarningar runtom i Sverige. ”Ge dig inte ut i trafiken i onödan eller förbered dig på att du kan bli stillastående” , skriver SMHI. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På torsdag och fredag varnar SMHI för snöfall. Redan i går kom gula varningar i delar av sydvästra Svealand, Värmland och längs Västerbottenskusten. Det handlar om delar av Västerbottens nordliga kustland, där bland annat Skellefteå ligger, där det kommer råda orange varning för snöfall från klockan 14 på torsdagen till klockan 23 på fredagen. – Det handlar främst om att det är första snön, vilket kan ställa till med bekymmer. Vi hade nog inte varnat för samma snöfall i januari eller februari, säger Kjell Lund, meteorolog SMHI. Snöfallet beskrivs som ”tidvis ymnigt” och väntas ge 20 till 30 centimeter snö. Lokalt kan det komma upp i 40 centimeter. SMHI uppmanar boende i området att inte ge sig ut i trafiken i onödan – då det kan vara svårt att ta sig fram ”på grund av snö på vägar, trafikolyckor eller stillastående fordon”. Även Trafikverket varnar att ”ymnigt snöfall” kan bidra till besvärligt väglag i det västerbottniska kustlandet och södra delarna av Norrland. ”Trafikanter uppmanas att undvika onödiga resor och för den som måste ge sig ut gäller det att vara förberedd på att du kan bli stillastående” , skriver Trafikverket i ett pressmeddelande. Kollektiv- och tågtrafik kan drabbas av förseningar och inställda avgångar. Tidigare i dag utökade SMHI även de gula varningarna – till Västernorrlands län och norra Hälsingland.

articles.title: Rödgröna partierna i hemligt möte: ”Bra samtal”
articles.summary: Bakom stängda dörrar möttes de rödgröna partierna i Tändstickspalatset i Stockholm under onsdagsförmiddagen. Partiledarna berättar om ”konstruktiva samtal”. Men Vänsterpartiets regeringskrav står fast. – Det finns inga nya besked i det avseendet, säger Nooshi Dadgostar.
articles.body_text: Bakom stängda dörrar möttes de rödgröna partierna i Tändstickspalatset i Stockholm under onsdagsförmiddagen. Partiledarna berättar om ”konstruktiva samtal”. Men Vänsterpartiets regeringskrav står fast. – Det finns inga nya besked i det avseendet, säger Nooshi Dadgostar. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Företrädare för rödgröna partier har mötts på det anrika Tändstickspalatset i centrala Stockholm under förmiddagen. Mötena ska enligt uppgifter till Expressen ha pågått sedan 10-tiden. Partiledare för såväl Vänsterpartiet som Miljöpartiet och Socialdemokraterna var på plats. – Vi har haft bra samtal, säger Magdalena Andersson. – Exakt vad vi diskuterar tror jag, för att föra processen framåt, är bäst att vi håller oss för oss själva. Huruvida det kommer inkomma ett ”totalpaket”, i enlighet med Elisabeth Thand Ringqvists förfrågan, är oklart. – Det är en av de många saker som diskuteras nu, säger Magdalena Andersson. Beskedet att hon önskar hålla Vänsterpartiet utanför regeringen står fast, enligt S-ledaren.

articles.title: Chatta med Expressen om regeringsbildningen
articles.summary: Max V Karlsson svarar på läsarnas frågor.
articles.body_text: Det var alla frågor vi hann med för i dag! Men vi återkommer, och jag tar med mig en drös frågeställningar till morgondagens avsnitt av Politikrummet. Tack snälla för alla engagerade och gedigna frågor, och tack för att du var med i chatten! Den omröstningen gällde en ren S-regering! Hehe, jag tycker att de gott kan bjuda in massmedia också. Total transparens! Skämt åsido handlar det också om att partierna vill kunna bygga relationer och förtroende utan insyn och inblandning från utomstående. Svårt att säga, men klart är att risken för rejäl huvudvärk i minoritetsställning är påtaglig. SD är inte alls sugna på en sådan lösning, och jag har inte hört att en sån ligger på bordet, så det tror jag är långt bort. Det är väl ändå jättemånga som ifrågasätter alla partiledarnas påståenden. Det ligger lite i politikens natur, med olika viljor, tänker jag. Inga beslut fattas i ren panik på den här nivån, är min bild. Hon gick fram med det för att hon såg det som alternativet med högst sannolikhet att samla tillräckligt stöd – nu får vi se om det håller. Det är väl många som skriver om det? Sen finns det skillnader i hur stora partierna är, men just vågmästarrollen är ju flitigt omtalad. MP och C står långt ifrån varandra när det gäller en hel del skogspolitik – men bägge partier ser ändå att det är betydligt lättare att samarbeta och att man ligger väldigt nära i andra frågor. Linjen mot V motiveras framför allt av sakpolitiska skillnader medan linjen mot SD beskrivs som både djupt ideologisk och sakpolitisk, är det korta svaret. Det finns väldigt mycket intressant läsning om hur mycket centerväljare ogillar SD hos valforskningsprogrammet på Göteborgs universitet, för den som vill veta mer! Jag vet inte riktigt vad du menar med hat, men både SD och V är särskilt utsatta när det gäller hot och hat mot företrädare. Jag tycker att det ska vara noll hat i politiken! Nepp, det kan vara hur många sonderingar som helst. Du tänker på statsministeromröstningar där det automatiskt blir extra val om den fjärde misslyckas.

articles.title: Minst fem C-distrikt säger nej till Kristersson, erfar Expressen
articles.summary: Centerpartiet är splittrat och tunga företrädare förordar olika lösningar för vägvalet. Vänster eller höger. – Det här är svårt, säger en C-källa.
articles.body_text: Minst fem C-distrikt säger nu tydligt nej till Kristerssons högeralternativ, erfar Expressen. – Det blir som att vi har ljugit väljarna rakt upp i ansiktet, säger en källa. Men partiet är splittrat och C-ledningen håller digitala möten löpande. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Senast på fredag klockan 17 vill C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist ha svar av Magdalena Andersson (S) och Ulf Kristersson (M). Hon har krävt att de levererar varsitt ”totalpaket” till C där de redovisar vilken regering de vill bilda och redogöra för den politik den ska föra. Stanna med de rödgröna eller återgå till den forna alliansen till höger. Expressen har tidigare avslöjat att splittringen kring vägvalet är stort i C-toppen. Partiledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist och partisekreteraren Hannes Hervieu uppfattas av källor i C luta åt högeralternativet, liksom C-studenter där de båda en gång varit aktiva. Thand Ringqvist själv har avfärdat uppgifterna. – Det finns ingenting jag föredrar, har hon tidigare sagt till Expressen, och samtidigt slagit fast att C:s röda linjer mot V och SD kvarstår. På den andra sidan anses kända riksdagsledamöter som Martin Ådahl, ekonomiskpolitisk talesperson, och Birgitta Ohlsson, tidigare L-minister som bytt parti till C, stå.

articles.title: Då kommer Sigtunaåtal – sex elever misstänks
articles.summary: Sigtuna humanistiska läroverket har skakats av en skandal med flera grova brott. – Jag kommer att väcka åtal nästa vecka, säger åklagare Lisa dos Santos.
articles.body_text: Sigtuna humanistiska läroverket har skakats av en skandal med flera grova brott. – Jag kommer att väcka åtal nästa vecka, säger åklagare Lisa dos Santos. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Flera elever misstänks för grova brott på internatet i Sigtuna. Under utredningens gång har en sjätte manlig elev i 18-årsåldern delgivits misstanke för bland annat misshandel, enligt åklagare Lisa dos Santos. Han har inte frihetsberövats. Ett stort antal förhör har hållits med elever och personal på skolan, enligt dos Santos. – Jag kommer att väcka åtal nästa vecka, det är planerat till den 19 november, säger hon. Är den sjätte eleven misstänkt för brott som har skett vid samma tillfälle som någon av de andra misstänkta? – Det kommer framgå i åtalet. Vissa personer är misstänkta för egen del och sen är det vissa brottsmisstankar där det finns fler personer involverade, säger hon. Totalt är nu sex misstänkta – alla manliga gymnasieelever i 18-årsåldern. Tre av dem greps i början av oktober och sitter häktade . De misstänks bland för grovt sexuellt ofredande, grovt olaga tvång och grov misshandel. Brotten ska ha begåtts på skolområdet mot andra elever. Ytterligare två personer delgavs misstanke i mitten av oktober – där en misstänks för misshandel och en för misshandel och olaga tvång. Flera elever har vittnat om en hård miljö på skolan med tystnadskultur, förnedringsritualer och poängsystem i en ”regelbok” med bestraffningar. Åklagaren har tidigare bekräftat att man beslagtagit en sådan bok i utredningen.

articles.body_text: Han försvarade den 45-årige man som dömdes för medhjälp till morden i Brattås. Inför förhandlingar i hovrätten byts han ut. Anledningen är att det uppstått ett jävsförhållande, rapporterar SVT Västernorrland. De nya uppgifterna är sekretessbelagda och utreds i en pågående förundersökning, men det har redan nu lett till att advokat Johan Lavås anses jävig i målet, och att han ”måste skiljas från uppdraget”. Ny försvarsadvokat från och med nu blir i stället Jonas Vedin. – Jag kan säga så mycket som att det här inte har något att göra med den tidigare försvararens agerande i målet på något sätt. Utan det rör sig om omständigheter i de nya uppgifterna som nu utreds, säger Jonas Vedin till SVT. I över 20 år var dubbelmordet på ett äldre par i Brattås ett mysterium för polisen. Till sist ledde dna-spår fram till en misstänkt gärningsman, som i september dömdes av Ångermanlands tingsrätt till 14 års fängelse för medhjälp till morden. (TT) Irans säkerhetschef Mohsen Rezaei hotar att slå till mot amerikanska militärbaser i Europa – om baserna används för att attackera Iran, rapporterar libanesisk tv. I ett utspel från Irans styre hotar landet att attackera militäranläggningar bortom Mellanöstern: – Om amerikanska flygplan lyfter från en amerikansk militärbas för att bomba Iran – även om det sker från en bas i ett europeiskt land eller i någon annan avlägsen region, kommer vi att slå till mot dessa baser, säger Mohsen Rezaei i en intervju med den libanesiska tv-kanalen Al Mayadeen. Rezaei gick med i Irans Revolutionsgarde 1980 och var dess högste befälhavare mellan 1981 och 1997. (TT) En person har förts till sjukhus efter en flerbilskrock på E20 utanför Strängnäs. Det rapporterar Ekuriren . Tre personer är inblandade i olyckan där en bil körde på en andra bakifrån. Vägen var avstängd tidigare på onsdagseftermiddagen. – En person är förd till sjukhus med ambulans, säger räddningstjänstens vakthavande befäl Jörgen Winborg till tidningen. Centerpartisten Niels Paarup-Petersen säger att C inte kommer att ge något besked i regeringsfrågan förrän de tagit del av de helhetspaket som efterfrågats av Moderaterna och Socialdemokraterna.
